deed: מנשה בן ישראל פנה לקרומוול בבקשה להחזיר את היהודים לאנגליה, והם חזרו אליה בשקט
title: Menasseh ben Israel, a rabbi from Amsterdam, appealed to Cromwell, and Jews returned to live openly in England

trailer.text: Menasseh ben Israel (1604–1657) was a Jewish rabbi, scholar, philosopher, diplomat and Hebrew printer, who devoted his life to teaching Judaism in Amsterdam.
In 1290 the edict expelling the Jews from England was issued.

According to Leeds University Library, in 1651 Menasseh began his campaign for the readmission of the Jews to England with an open letter to Oliver Cromwell, the Lord Protector, published under the title The Humble Adresses.
In 1655 he went to England himself, to argue for formal recognition of Jewish settlement there.

According to the Cromwell Association, no formal decision was made, but it soon became clear that the presence of Jews would be more openly tolerated, and according to Rabone, by December 1656 a synagogue had already been established in Cree-Church Lane.

glance.label: In London
glance.value: Presented Humble Addresses in person to the Council of State at Whitehall, 31 October 1655.

glance.label: What came afterwards
glance.value: A synagogue in Cree-Church Lane (1656), a cemetery at Mile End (1657)

paragraphs.text: On 18 July 1290 the edict expelling the Jews from England was issued.
According to Lucien Wolf, writing in 1901, for two centuries after the expulsion by Edward I, England was, for the Jewish people, little more than a bitter memory.
According to Rabbi Jeremy Gordon, Jews had never entirely left.
In his words, in the aftermath of the expulsions from Spain and Portugal several hundred conversos came to trade in London.
According to the Cromwell Association, even before 1655 an established Jewish community lived in London, presenting itself as Spanish merchants for fear of persecution.

stations.title: A boy from Lisbon who became a rabbi in Amsterdam

paragraphs.text: According to Lawrence Rabone, Menasseh was born in 1604 in Lisbon and was baptised with the Christian name Manoel Dias Soeiro.
According to Wolf, his father was a Marrano of Lisbon who had suffered at the hands of the Inquisition, and as a result settled in Amsterdam.
According to Rabone, Menasseh escaped the Inquisition in Portugal in his youth and arrived in Amsterdam in 1613 or 1614.
According to Rabone, after the death of Rabbi Isaac Uziel, Menasseh was appointed rabbi of the Neveh Shalom synagogue, when he was only around eighteen years of age.
In 1626/7 he set up his own printing press, and was the first Jew to print books in Hebrew in Amsterdam.
According to The Jewish Press, his 1632 book El Conciliador was among the first books written by a Jew in a modern language that were also of interest to Christian readers.
According to the Jewish Press, his acquaintances and correspondents included Queen Christina of Sweden, the painter Rembrandt and the statesman Hugo Grotius.
In 1642, when the Prince of Orange and Henrietta Maria, Queen of England, visited the synagogue in Amsterdam, Menasseh delivered a welcome speech.
According to Wolf, in the speech he praised the queen of Charles I, and at first he apparently leaned towards the Royalist side.

stations.title: Testimony from Quito and a book called "The Hope of Israel"

paragraphs.text: In 1644 Antonio de Montezinos, a marrano who had returned from Quito, testified under oath before Menasseh that he had met Israelites of the tribe of Reuben.
Menasseh was convinced, and the public discussion that followed led to his becoming known in England.

According to Rabone, Menasseh was inspired to write "The Hope of Israel" by two letters he received late in 1648 from the millenarian John Dury, who had asked him only for a letter; instead, Menasseh wrote a book.
According to Wolf, in the autumn of 1649 a letter he received from John Dury, a well-known English Puritan, suggested a course of action to Menasseh.
According to Wolf, in January 1649 a petition from Johanna and Ebenezer Cartwright, Baptists of Amsterdam, to repeal the law of expulsion was presented to Lord Fairfax and the Council of Officers.
In 1650 Menasseh published "The Hope of Israel" (Mikveh Israel), intended primarily for a Gentile audience and published simultaneously in English and Latin, in Latin under the title Spes Israelis.
Menasseh wrote in 1656 that he had dedicated the book to the first Parliament and the Council of State.
According to Wolf, the tract made a profound impression throughout England, and Puritans were enthusiastic that an eminent Jewish rabbi was blessing the Republican government.

stations.title: A letter to Cromwell and a journey to London

paragraphs.text: According to Leeds University Library, in 1651 Menasseh began his campaign for the readmission of the Jews to England with an open letter to Oliver Cromwell, the Lord Protector, published under the title The Humble Adresses.
According to Leeds Library, the work was first published in Amsterdam in 1651 and reprinted in London in 1655.

According to Leeds Library, Menasseh believed that the rule of the Puritans offered a unique opportunity to reverse the expulsion, and he sought to convince Cromwell that the settlement of the Jews would hasten universal redemption.
Menasseh himself wrote that he understood the verse about one end of the earth to the other end of the earth to mean that the end of the earth is the British island.
On 10 April 1656 he wrote that for seven years he had worked without pause, by letters and other means, for the admission of the Jews to England.
In 1655 Menasseh went to England to argue for formal recognition of Jewish settlement there.
The leaders of the Sephardi community in Amsterdam tried to dissuade him from the journey, and when he went nevertheless, they removed him from his post.
Menasseh wrote that he parted from his home, his friends and his relatives and set out for England.
According to the Cromwell Association, he arrived in London with a delegation and members of his family, and personally petitioned Cromwell to readmit the Jews.
According to Raboon, on 31 October 1655 Menasseh presented his work Humble Addresses in person to the Council of State at Whitehall.
According to the Cromwell Association, the petition requested citizenship, freedom of worship, burial grounds, freedom to trade and the withdrawal of all laws against Jews.
According to Rabbi Gordon, Menasseh also raised less spiritual arguments, and devoted several pages to a survey of the profitability of the Jewish nation in various countries that had admitted Jews.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Cromwell sent for Menasseh, and in 1655 a motion on the admission of the Jews was introduced in the Council.
According to the Encyclopedia, Cromwell supported the admission of the Jews partly in the hope of fulfilling a messianic prophecy, and mainly because they had aided him.
According to the Jewish Press, he was sympathetic to the Jewish cause because of his Puritan views, his tolerant leanings and his understanding that Jewish merchants would benefit English commerce.
On 4 December 1655 Cromwell opened the Whitehall Conference.
Menasseh wrote that Cromwell convened at Whitehall divines, lawyers and merchants of different opinions.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the conference included representatives of the army, the law and trade, and sixteen divines.
According to Worden, over the following fortnight five meetings were held, the last of them open to the public.
According to Rabone, the lawyers at the conference saw no legal reason to prevent Jewish settlement in England.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the conference determined that the expulsion of 1290 had never been valid.
According to Rabone, the merchants were largely opposed, and the clergy were divided.
According to Rabbi Gordon, opponents spread rumours of child-murder, the recurring blood libels.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, on 18 December a hostile crowd burst into the Council Chamber, and Cromwell vacated the chair and brought the proceedings to a close.
According to Rabbi Gordon, Cromwell disbanded the conference before it could report.
According to Leeds Library, the conference concluded that Jewish settlement was legal, but no official declaration or settlement privilege was issued.
John Evelyn recorded in his diary on 14 December 1655 that the Jews had been admitted.
According to Worden, the opposition at the conference did not prevent Cromwell from conniving at the open presence of Jews in England.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, in 1656, after the outbreak of war with Spain, the Marranos threw off their disguise and appeared openly as Jews.
In 1656 the merchant Antonio Rodrigues Robles was at the centre of the matter.
According to the Jewish Press, that year Cromwell gave a verbal promise, backed by the Council of State in the Robles case, to allow Jews to return and practise their faith freely.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Cromwell gave Menasseh a grant of £100.
According to Rabbi Gordon, there is no Act of Parliament that formally readmitted the Jews.
Menasseh wrote in April 1656 that no final decision had yet been received from His Highness.
According to the Cromwell Association, no formal decision was made, but it soon became clear that the presence of Jews would be more openly tolerated.
According to Rabone, by December 1656 a synagogue was established in a house in Cree-Church Lane, and in 1657 the Sephardi cemetery at Mile End opened.

stations.title: The rabbi who did not see the end

paragraphs.text: In 1656 Samuel, Menasseh's son, died in England and was buried in Middelburg.
According to Worden, Menasseh, who had mobilised support from Amsterdam for eight years, was broken by the apparent failure of his mission.
According to Rabone, Menasseh died on 20 November 1657 in Middelburg, and his body was brought to Amsterdam and buried in the Jewish cemetery at Ouderkerk.
According to Rabone, he never lived to see a formal declaration of the admission of the Jews.
Lucien Wolf wrote in 1901 that Menasseh's name would always hold the chief place on the first page of the history of the present Anglo-Jewish community.
According to Rabone, Menasseh's influence on the Christian world was greater than his influence on the Jewish world.
William Prynne published the hostile pamphlet "Short Demurrer" in response.
According to Leeds Library, Prynne was a conservative Puritan lawyer and an opponent of Cromwell, who mixed learning with gross stereotypes in his pamphlet.
In 1656 Menasseh published Vindiciae Judaeorum in English, in which he refuted six anti-Jewish myths, among them the blood libel and the claim that Jews are idolaters.
According to Wolf, the Member of Parliament Sir Edward Spencer agreed to the admission of the Jews on conditions designed to strengthen those who also demanded their conversion to Christianity.
The question of how much of the achievement belongs to Menasseh himself remains open.

disagreements.question: When did John Dury's letters arrive?

versions.says: According to Rabone: two letters arrived late in 1648
According to Wolf: the letter arrived in the autumn of 1649

disagreements.question: In what year did Menasseh arrive in London?

versions.says: According to Raboon: in September 1655, near Rosh Hashanah
According to the Cromwell Association: in September 1655, with a delegation and members of his family

disagreements.question: How far was Menasseh the decisive factor in the readmission?

versions.says: According to Wolf: Cromwell was the mainspring of the whole movement, and Menasseh was a puppet in his hands
According to the Cromwell Association: the significance of Menasseh's mission in achieving the toleration of 1656 is still a matter of discussion

disagreements.question: When did the campaign for the return of the Jews begin?

versions.says: According to Worden: the campaign began in earnest in 1649
Menasseh himself wrote in April 1656 that he had worked for seven years without pause
According to Worden: Menasseh mobilised support from Amsterdam for eight years

disagreements.question: How many Jews lived in England before the readmission?

versions.says: According to Rabbi Gordon: several hundred conversos who came to trade in London
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia: in 1653 about twenty Marrano families lived in England

disagreements.question: When, and to what position, was Menasseh appointed at the Neveh Shalom synagogue?

versions.says: According to Rabone: after Uziel's death in 1622, appointed rabbi of the synagogue, at around eighteen
According to Leeds Library: appointed preacher (predicador) in 1628, and hakham (rabbi) only in 1631

claims.text: מנשה בן ישראל (1604–1657) היה רב יהודי, חוקר, פילוסוף, דיפלומט ומדפיס עברית.
claims.quote: Menasseh ben Israel, rabbi, scholar, philosopher, diplomat and Hebrew printer, 1604-1657

claims.text: לפי לורנס ראבון, מנשה בן ישראל נמלט מהאינקוויזיציה בפורטוגל בנעוריו, התיישב באמסטרדם והקדיש את שארית חייו להוראת היהדות.
claims.quote: Having escaped the furnace of the Inquisition in Portugal in his youth, he settled in Amsterdam and spent the rest of his life teaching Judaism.

claims.text: ב-18 ביולי 1290 הוצא צו הגירוש של היהודים מאנגליה.
claims.quote: On July 18, 1290, the Edict of Expulsion was issued.

claims.text: לפי ספריית אוניברסיטת לידס, ב-1651 פתח מנשה בקמפיין להחזרת היהודים לאנגליה במכתב פתוח לאוליבר קרומוול.
claims.quote: 1651: Menasseh initiates his campaign for the re-admission of the Jews to England by writing an open letter to Oliver Cromwell.

claims.text: ב-1655 יצא מנשה לאנגליה כדי לטעון להכרה רשמית בהתיישבות יהודית שם.
claims.quote: 1655: He departs for England, to argue his case for the formal recognition of Jewish resettlement in England.

claims.text: לפי אגודת קרומוול, לא התקבלה החלטה רשמית להתיר את החזרה, אך התברר במהרה שנוכחות היהודים תיסבל בגלוי יותר.
claims.quote: There was no formal decision to allow readmission but it was soon evident that the presence of Jews would be more openly tolerated.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, עד דצמבר 1656 הוקם בית כנסת בבית ברחוב קרי-צ'רץ' ובית הקברות הספרדי במייל אנד נפתח ב-1657.
claims.quote: Nevertheless, by December 1656, a synagogue was established in a house in Cree-Church Lane and the Sephardi Velho cemetery opened on Mile End Road in 1657.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, מנשה נולד ב-1604 בליסבון ונטבל בשם הנוצרי מנואל דיאס סוארו.
claims.quote: Menasseh ben Israel was born in 1604 in Lisbon. He was baptised and given the Christian name Manoel

claims.text: לפי ראבון, ב-31 באוקטובר 1655 הציג מנשה את חיבורו "Humble Addresses" באופן אישי בפני מועצת המדינה בווייטהול.
claims.quote: on 31 October 1655, he presented this pamphlet in person to the Council of State at Whitehall.

claims.text: לפי לוסיאן וולף (1901), במשך שתי מאות שנה אחרי הגירוש הגדול בידי אדוארד הראשון הייתה אנגליה בעיני העם היהודי כמעט רק זיכרון מר.
claims.quote: for two centuries after the Great Expulsion by Edward I., little more than a bitter memory to the Jewish people

claims.text: לפי הרב ג'רמי גורדון, היהודים מעולם לא עזבו לגמרי: בעקבות הגירושים מספרד ופורטוגל הגיעו ללונדון לסחור כמה מאות קונברסוס.
claims.quote: In truth, however, Jews had never entirely left. In the aftermath of expulsions from Spain and Portugal several hundred conversos (New Christians) came to trade in London.

claims.text: לפי אגודת קרומוול, קיימת עדות לקהילה יהודית מבוססת בלונדון עוד לפני 1655, שחיה כסוחרים ספרדים מחשש לרדיפה.
claims.quote: there is evidence of an established Jewish community in London before 1655. Fearful of persecution they did not declare their identity, living as Spanish merchants.

claims.text: לפי וולף, מנשה היה בנו של מראנו מליסבון שסבל מידי האינקוויזיציה ובעקבות זאת השתקע באמסטרדם.
claims.quote: Menasseh ben Israel was the son of a Marrano of Lisbon, who had suffered at the hands of the Inquisition, and had, as a result, taken up his abode in Amsterdam.

claims.quote: When Chacham Uziel died in 1620, R’ Menashe was proclaimed rabbi of the Sephardic community at the astonishingly young age of 18

claims.quote: Cromwell was especially sympathetic to the Jewish cause due to his Puritan views, more tolerant leanings, and pragmatic view that the Jewish merchant would benefit English commerce.

claims.text: ב-4 בדצמבר 1655 פתח קרומוול את ועידת וייטהול.
claims.quote: On 4 December 1655, Oliver Cromwell opened a conference summoned

claims.text: מנשה כתב ב-1656 שקרומוול כינס אסיפה בווייטהול של אנשי דת, משפטנים וסוחרים בעלי דעות שונות.
claims.quote: Whereupon it pleased His Highnesse to convene an Assembly at Whitehall, of Divines, Lawyers, and Merchants, of different persuasions, and opinions.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, בוועידה השתתפו נציגי הצבא, המשפט והמסחר ושישה עשר אנשי דת.
claims.quote: It consisted of representatives of the army, the law, the trading interests, and sixteen divines

claims.text: לפי בלייר וורדן, במהלך השבועיים שלאחר מכן התקיימו חמש ישיבות, האחרונה פתוחה לציבור, ואז הוועידה נדחתה.
claims.quote: During the next fortnight five meetings were held, the last of them open to the public, before the convention was adjourned.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, עורכי הדין בוועידה לא ראו כל סיבה משפטית למנוע התיישבות יהודים באנגליה.
claims.quote: The lawyers saw no legal reason why Jews could not settle in England.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, הוועידה קבעה שהגירוש של 1290 מעולם לא היה תקף.
claims.quote: this was settled by the decision that the expulsion of 1290 had never been valid.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, הסוחרים התנגדו ברובם לקבלת היהודים, ואנשי הדת היו חלוקים.
claims.quote: By contrast, the merchants were largely opposed to readmission, whilst the clergy were divided on the merits of readmission.

claims.text: לפי הרב גורדון, מתנגדים הפיצו שמועות על רצח ילדים, כלומר עלילות הדם החוזרות.
claims.quote: Others spread rumours of child-murder, the recurring blood libel accusations.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, ב-18 בדצמבר פרץ לאולם המועצה המון עוין.
claims.quote: Finally, on Dec. 18, a hostile crowd thronged into the Council Chamber

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, קרומוול עזב את הכיסא וסיים את הדיונים, והוועידה התפזרה ללא מחאה.
claims.quote: he vacated the chair and brought the proceedings to a close. The conference was cowed, and dissolved without a word of protest.

claims.text: לפי הרב גורדון, קרומוול פיזר את הוועידה לפני שהספיקה להגיש דוח.
claims.quote: Cromwell disbanded the conference before it could report.

claims.text: לפי ספריית לידס, הוועידה הסיקה שהתיישבות יהודית חוקית, אך לא ניתנה הצהרה רשמית או זכות התיישבות.
claims.quote: It concludes that Jewish settlement is legally admissible, but no official declaration or settlement privilege is issued.

claims.text: ג'ון אבלין רשם ביומנו ב-14 בדצמבר 1655 שהיהודים התקבלו.
claims.quote: John Evelyn even entered in his diary under the date December 14, 1655

claims.text: לפי וורדן, ההתנגדות בוועידה לא מנעה מקרוממל להעלים עין מנוכחותם הגלויה של יהודים באנגליה.
claims.quote: it did not prevent Cromwell from conniving at the open presence of Jews in England

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, ב-1656, לאחר פרוץ המלחמה עם ספרד, זרקו המראנוס את המסווה והופיעו בגלוי כיהודים.
claims.quote: in 1656, relying upon the decision that the expulsion of 1290 was no longer valid, they openly threw off their disguise and assumed the position of Jews.

claims.text: לפי הרב גורדון, ב-1656 נעצר הסוחר אנטוניו רודריגס רובלס כפאפיסט, ונמלט מעונש כשטען שהוא יהודי; קרומוול התערב.
claims.quote: Robles was threatened with sequestration of his considerable assets and only escaped punishment when he claimed that, rather than being a papist, he was actually Jewish.

claims.text: לפי ה-Jewish Press, רכושו של רובלס הוחרם כרכוש של נתין אויב עם פרוץ המלחמה בספרד ב-1656, והוא זכה בפטור בטענה שהוא פורטוגלי ולא ספרדי.
claims.quote: When his property was seized as that of an enemy alien after the outbreak of war with Spain in 1656, he successfully obtained an exemption

claims.text: לפי ה-Jewish Press, ב-1656 ניתן הבטחה בעל פה מקרומוול, בגיבוי מועצת המדינה במקרה רובלס, לאפשר ליהודים לחזור ולקיים את דתם בחופשיות.
claims.quote: in 1656 a verbal promise from Cromwell, backed by the Council of State in the Robles case, to allow Jews to return to England and freely practice their faith

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, קרומוול העניק למנשה בן ישראל מענק של 100 לירות.
claims.quote: He had previously made a grant of £100 to Manasseh ben Israel.

claims.text: לפי הרב גורדון, לא קיים חוק של הפרלמנט שקיבל רשמית את היהודים בחזרה.
claims.quote: There is no Act of Parliament officially welcoming them back.

claims.text: מנשה כתב באפריל 1656 שעדיין לא התקבלה החלטה סופית מהוד רוממותו.
claims.quote: Insomuch, that as yet, we have had no finall determination from his most Serene Highnesse.

claims.text: ב-1656 מת באנגליה בנו של מנשה, שמואל, ונקבר במידלבורג.
claims.quote: His son Samuel dies in England, and is buried in Middelburg.

claims.text: לפי וורדן, מנשה, שגייס תמיכה מאמסטרדם שמונה שנים, נשבר מכישלונה הנראה של שליחותו.
claims.quote: Menasseh ben Israel, who from his base in Amsterdam had for eight years been mobilising support for the readmission of the Jews to England, was broken by the apparent failure of his mission.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, מנשה מת ב-20 בנובמבר 1657 במידלבורג וגופתו הובאה לאמסטרדם ונקברה בבית הקברות היהודי באודרקרק.
claims.quote: He died on 20 November 1657 in Middleburg. His body was subsequently brought to Amsterdam and he was buried in the Jewish cemetery at Ouderkerk.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, מנשה לא זכה לראות הכרזה רשמית על קבלת היהודים.
claims.quote: Menasseh never lived to see a formal declaration of readmission.

claims.text: לפי וולף (1901), שמו של מנשה יישאר תמיד במקום הראשון בדפי ההיסטוריה של הקהילה האנגלו-יהודית.
claims.quote: whose name must always hold the chief place on the first page of the history of the present Anglo-Jewish community.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, השפעתו של מנשה על העולם הנוצרי הייתה גדולה מהשפעתו על העולם היהודי.
claims.quote: It is noteworthy that he had more of an impact on the Gentile world than the Jewish world

claims.text: ויליאם פרין פרסם בתגובה את החיבור העוין "Short Demurrer".
claims.quote: William Prynne issues his hostile Short Demurrer in response.

claims.text: לפי ספריית לידס, פרין היה עורך דין פוריטני שמרן ויריב של קרומוול, שערבב בחיבורו לימוד עם סטריאוטיפים גסים.
claims.quote: Prynne, a conservative Puritan lawyer and opponent of Cromwell, mixed his learning with gross stereotypes.

claims.text: ב-1656 פרסם מנשה באנגלית את "Vindiciae Judaeorum" והפריך בו שישה מיתוסים אנטי-יהודיים, ובהם עלילת הדם והטענה שהיהודים עובדי אלילים.
claims.quote: Written in English, Menasseh confuted six anti-Jewish myths: the blood libel; the charge that Jews are idolaters

claims.text: לפי וולף, חבר הפרלמנט סר אדוארד ספנסר הסכים לקבלת היהודים בתנאי שנועדו לחזק את אלה שדרשו גם המרתם לנצרות.
claims.quote: he expressed his readiness to agree to the admission of the Jews on twelve conditions artfully designed to strengthen the hands of the sectaries

claims.text: לפי וולף, קרומוול היה הכוח המניע של כל המהלך ומנשה היה בובה בידיו.
claims.quote: there is ample evidence that he was the mainspring of the whole movement, and that Menasseh was but a puppet in his hands

claims.text: לפי אגודת קרומוול, חשיבות שליחותו של מנשה להשגת רמת הסובלנות ב-1656 היא עדיין נושא לדיון.
claims.quote: The significance of the mission by Menasseh ben Israel in achieving the level of toleration reached in 1656 is a continuing discussion.

claims.text: לפי ראבון, מנשה הגיע ללונדון בספטמבר 1655, סמוך לראש השנה.
claims.quote: Menasseh arrived in London just before Rosh Hashanah in September 1655

claims.text: לפי וורדן, הקמפיין להחזרת היהודים החל ברצינות ב-1649 והגיע לשיאו בחודש האחרון של 1655.
claims.quote: It was no coincidence that the campaign for Jewish readmission, which began in earnest in 1649, reached its peak in the last month of 1655.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, ב-1653 חיו באנגליה כעשרים משפחות מראנוס שברחו מספרד מחשש לאינקוויזיציה.
claims.quote: There were at this time (1653) about twenty Marano families settled in England, who had fled from Spain through fear of the Inquisition.

claims.text: לפי ראבון: אחרי מות אוזיאל ב-1622 מונה לרב בית הכנסת, כבן שמונה עשרה
claims.quote: Menasseh was appointed rabbi of the Neveh Shalom synagogue, despite being only around eighteen years of age
claims.checker_note: audit: page could not be fetched by script; verifier quoted it

claims.text: לפי ספריית לידס: מונה לדרשן (פרדיקדור) ב-1628, ולחכם (רב) רק ב-1631
claims.quote: having been appointed predicador (preacher) there in 1628
